references.text: The command to tear down the altars of the nations and destroy their idols, which explains how the Israelites were to remove idolatry.
Describes the high places and green trees where idol worship took place in Israel during King Rehoboam's reign.
Mentions the high places and Asherah poles under every green tree, showing how the Israelites broke this commandment.
The prophet Jeremiah accuses the people of idol worship under every green tree, directly referencing the places that were to be destroyed.
Ezekiel describes idol worship on the high hills and under the green trees where Israel offered incense to their idols.
King Ahaz sacrificed on the hills and under every green tree, in direct opposition to this commandment.
Describes how Israel set up pillars and Asherah poles on the hills and under the green trees, which led to exile.
Isaiah condemns those who burn with desire under the terebinths and every green tree, showing continued idol worship.
